source.title: Count the Number of Houses at a Certain Distance I

teaching.hint: How many times could a shortest route benefit from crossing the single extra street?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A shortest route uses the extra edge at most once, so its distance is the minimum of a direct path and two orientations through that edge.
solution_outline.approach: Enumerate every unordered pair of distinct houses. Compare path distance with the route entering the extra edge at `x` and the route entering at `y`, then add two to the appropriate distance bucket.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Each processed unordered pair contributes exactly its two ordered directions to the bucket for its true shortest distance.
solution_outline.correctness: Repeating the extra edge creates a removable loop, so an optimal route is among the three evaluated forms. All unordered pairs are visited once and every ordered pair is counted once.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n²)` time and `O(n)` output space, with constant auxiliary state.
solution_outline.pitfall: Counting each unordered pair only once undercounts the required ordered pairs by a factor of two.

common_wrong_turns: Ignore the reverse orientation through the extra street
source_fidelity_notes: The source uses a 1-indexed result convention; this brief states the returned array index explicitly and clarifies distinct ordered houses.
